## Reasoning effort

A r
easoning effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**, not a free-standing\nfield. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `source`,
an optional `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallback`) carries it as `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is\naccepted everywhe

re a model choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.mode
lSelection` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |\n| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure
-adhoc`) | `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |\n| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`, read
back on the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`, read ba
*Levels.** `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of\n them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEffo
rts` on each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for\n that model —
do not guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded
on the execution record, or refused with\n `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling\n temperature.
\n* **A selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone i
t pins its own model. A bare model\n change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model\n instead of fai
ling.\n* **Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the ca
se's existing selection for that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.\n* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on
a client `set`, an environment\n or a suite, keeping the bare model id.\n* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential fiel

d; an unknown key
 (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.
* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`
 rep
orts `modelSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never ap

plied, so
 writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored
 value is refused by the runner.

`
POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a\nper-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on t
he session's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a\n`hostId`'s saved selection c
arries, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.\n\nThe SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operatio
ns:\n`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits the selection the target\nalready has, and is refused (`send modelSe

lection`) when there is none.

## Not in the API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** available over t

he API
today (most exist in the hosted inspector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design — see [Authentication

then upload the token to one of the server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Discord](ht

tps://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) — it directly shapes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-ve
rsioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **During the
preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overvi
ew.md).\n* **Additive changes** — new endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes — are consid
ered non-breaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.\n* Error **codes** are stable identifiers

; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario`
is\n**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the\noperation names, the SDK types and the noun-be

aring response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{proj
ectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{s
tudyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/pr
ojects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{ru
nId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../go
als-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarm

RunId}/insights` |

Response fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRu

nId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`get_user
_testing_scenario` served the environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fi

elds are
absent rather than null when you may not have them.
